extracted.intended_audience: researchers in cognitive neuroscience / neuroaesthetics and mathematically trained readers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and analysing an fMRI experiment that correlates subjective ratings of mathematical ‘beauty’ and understanding with brain activity in mathematician subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection / expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects were mathematicians at postgraduate or postdoctoral level (16 recruited; one excluded), recruited from colleges in London; all had normal or corrected-to-normal vision and gave written informed consent; study approved by the University College London Ethics Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the study aims to separate understanding from aesthetic response, participants needed fairly advanced knowledge of mathematics so they could comprehend and rate the formulae. Non-mathematicians were also given questionnaires but were not scanned because lack of understanding made the main analyses infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion criteria and handling of medication/diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: One subject was eliminated after it transpired he suffered from attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and had been on medication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude subjects whose clinical conditions or medication could affect neural responses or task performance; report exclusions and confirm they do not change overall results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus set and pre-exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Sixty mathematical formulae were provided to each subject ~2–3 weeks before scanning for study at leisure (Data Sheet 1: EquationsForm.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-exposure allows subjects to form stable pre-scan beauty ratings used to balance stimuli during scanning; provide a data sheet of equations so others can reproduce stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-scan beauty rating scale and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects rated each of the 60 equations before scanning on a scale from −5 (ugly) to +5 (beautiful). Pre-scan ratings were used to balance the sequence of stimuli for each subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-scan ratings to divide the 60 equations into three groups (20 low, 20 medium, 20 high) for each subject and to pseudo-randomize presentation so that preferred and non-preferred equations are evenly distributed across sessions and not presented consecutively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scan-time beauty rating categories
rubrics_metrics.description: During scanning subjects re-rated the same equations on an abridged three-category scale: Ugly, Neutral, or Beautiful (coded −1, 0, 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scan-time categorical ratings provide the parametric modulator (after coding) and allow both parametric and categorical analyses; note that categorical analysis is less sensitive than parametric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-scan understanding ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: A few days after scanning subjects reported their level of understanding of each equation on a numerical scale from 0 (no understanding) to 3 (profound understanding), and described subjective/emotional responses (Data Sheet 2: UnderstandingForm.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-scan understanding ratings are used as a second parametric modulator to dissociate neural effects of understanding from beauty; the imperfect correlation between understanding and beauty is necessary to separate their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus presentation timing and session structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Four functional scanning sessions; each session displayed 15 equations (so each of the 60 appeared once across sessions). Each session started with a 19.5 s blank, then 15 trials each of 16 s (equation display), interspersed with four blanks of 16–17 s for baseline; trial structure: equation displayed 16 s, 1 s blank, 3 s response period, then 1–2 s inter-trial blank; session ended with a 30 s blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize trials and blanks to acquire baseline signal, allow T1 equilibration, and permit rest between sessions. Use pre-scan ratings to ensure each session contains 5 low-, 5 medium-, and 5 high-rated equations and avoid sequential repetition of same-rated equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus visual/display parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Equations generated with Cogent 2000 and displayed by an Epson projector (1600×1200, 60 Hz) back-projected onto a translucent screen viewed via an angled mirror; equations drawn in same sized white font on a fixed grey background; visual angle and brightness values specified (width 4°–24°, height 1°–5°; screen brightness varied 280–324 cd/m^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep font, color, background, and brightness consistent across stimuli to avoid low-level visual confounds; record exact display hardware and visual angles for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters and hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Scans acquired on a 3-T Siemens Magnetom Trio MRI scanner with 32-channel head volume coil. A B0 fieldmap was acquired and echo-planar imaging (EPI) applied for functional scans measuring BOLD signals (echo time TE = 30 ms; volume time reported as 3.264 s; 48 axial slices, 2 mm thick with 1 mm gap, voxel resolution ~3×3×3 mm). High-resolution T1 anatomical scan (MDEFT) also acquired (176 slices, 1 mm isotropic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report scanner model, coil, sequence parameters (TE, TR/volume time, slice thickness, gaps, voxel resolution), and anatomical scan protocol to allow reproducibility and comparison across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-scan balancing of stimulus sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-scan beauty ratings were used to divide the 60 equations into 20 low-, 20 medium-, and 20 high-rated equations for each subject; sequences were pseudo-randomized so that each session contained 5 of each rating and no two same-rated equations occurred consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing ensures even distribution of subjective categories across sessions and reduces confounds due to stimulus order; document how pseudo-randomization is implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis software and modelling approach
rubrics_metrics.description: SPM8 (Statistical Parametric Mapping) was used. At the single-subject level the understanding rating (0–3) and the scan-time beauty rating (coded −1, 0, 1) were included as first and second parametric modulators (boxcar modelling appearance of each equation). Orthogonalization was used so that the beauty modulator captures variance not explained by understanding and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parametric modulators and orthogonalization to dissociate correlated subjective variables (beauty vs understanding). Explain the order of modulators and implications: the second modulator can only capture variance unexplained by the first, leaving a common portion unassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric vs categorical analyses and their sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Parametric analyses look for relationships between BOLD signal and rated quantities on an individual session basis and allow isolation via orthogonalization; categorical analyses average BOLD signal for each category across sessions and subjects but are less sensitive and cannot separate orthogonalized components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer parametric analyses to detect graded relationships and to separate correlated factors using orthogonalization; use categorical analyses as supplementary checks to obtain parameter estimates per category while noting reduced sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjunction-null analysis to test overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: A conjunction-null analysis (Nichols et al., 2005) was used to determine overlap within mOFC between regions showing parametric activation with beauty and regions showing general de-activation produced by viewing mathematical formulae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conjunction-null inference when testing whether two contrasts share overlapping activations; specify thresholding consistently for both contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thresholding and correction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Main contrasts reported at cluster-level significance with familywise error correction over whole brain (P_Clust-FWE < 0.05) as reported by SPM8 using random field theory; background uncorrected threshold P_unc < 0.001 and extent threshold of 10 voxels used to define clusters. For other contrasts not of principal interest, report activations surviving a peak-voxel threshold of P_FWE < 0.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare and apply correction procedures (cluster-level FWE, peak-voxel FWE where appropriate), uncorrected thresholds for cluster formation, and minimum extent thresholds. Report when activations do not reach significance but may be of interest for future studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and interpretation of non-significant activations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some activations that did not reach significance were nevertheless reported as they suggest areas which may contribute to the main activation; the authors note that whether they do will be left to future studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report subthreshold effects with caution, clearly label them as not significant, and propose future work to test their role rather than over-interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling imbalance in behavioural categories
rubrics_metrics.description: There were fewer 'Ugly' than 'Neutral' or 'Beautiful' ratings; in two sessions there was no 'Ugly' rating. Authors state this imbalance does not bias estimation/inference about effects of beauty—it reduces efficiency but still allowed identification of significant effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and quantify imbalances in categorical counts; discuss impacts on efficiency and sensitivity but argue whether bias is introduced. Where possible, design stimuli/subject groups to avoid extreme imbalances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of beauty and understanding effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Because beauty and understanding ratings correlated but imperfectly, separate parametric modulators and orthogonalization were used to distinguish activations that correlate with beauty alone versus those with understanding alone. The remaining common variance cannot be directly attributed to either component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When subjective measures correlate, explicitly model them together and use orthogonalization to isolate unique variance; explicitly discuss the unavoidable shared variance and its interpretational limits.
